  "source": "Bernstein",
  "title": "AI Data Center Interconnects: Copper Inside, Optical Outside, CPO in Between (webinar recap)",
  "type": "sector",
  "priority": "medium",
  "published": "2026-10-18",
  "insights": [
   "AI workloads are fundamentally altering data center interconnect architecture, shifting requirements from traditional copper-heavy designs to a mix of copper for short-reach scale-up and single-mode optics for long-reach scale-out.",
   "The industry framework is 'copper inside, optics outside, CPO in between,' with copper remaining the dominant medium for short-reach rack connectivity due to cost and technical viability.",
   "Physics limits copper reach as signaling speeds increase; passive copper reach compresses to ~18 inches at 200Gbps and ~12 inches at 400Gbps, necessitating a transition to optics for longer distances.",
   "Co-packaged optics (CPO) addresses switch-level constraints by moving electrical-to-optical conversion adjacent to the switch silicon, reducing the electrical path from ~18 inches to ~0.5 inches.",
   "CPO adoption is expected to be gradual, with meaningful practical adoption starting from 2030+ as the manufacturing ecosystem for silicon photonics matures.",
   "Alternative architectures like co-packaged copper (CPC) and near-packaged optics (NPO) are developing in parallel to solve front-panel density and reach challenges.",
   "Inference workloads do not inherently require optics inside the rack today, and copper should continue to be used where bandwidth and reach allow.",
   "The supply chain for indium-phosphide lasers is a potential bottleneck, as ~70% of supply originates from China and AI build-outs are placing significantly greater demands on manufacturing yields."
